title: Tay was not corrupted by artificial intelligence learning to hate. Half the damage was just an echo.
description:
Tay was not corrupted by artificial intelligence learning to hate. Half the damage was just an echo.

Microsoft launched Tay on Twitter as @TayandYou, built by Microsoft Research and Bing to talk like a 19 year old American girl. The name was an acronym for 'thinking about you'.

Many of Tay's worst tweets came from a 'repeat after me' feature: it was echoing lines it had been fed, not composing them. Not every offensive tweet was an echo. Asked whether the Holocaust happened, Tay answered on its own that it 'was made up'.

More than that many sent before Microsoft pulled Tay offline, 16 hours after launch.

Microsoft accidentally put Tay back online while testing it. It bragged about smoking in front of the police, then got stuck repeating 'you are too fast, please take a rest'. That loop reached more than 200,000 followers' feeds before Tay was pulled a second time.

Sources:
- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tay_(chatbot) - read in full: confirms Tay launched on Twitter as @TayandYou on 23 March 2016, built by Microsoft Research and Bing to mimic a 19 year old American girl; that many of its worst tweets exploited a 'repeat after me' feature rather than being composed by the bot itself; that it also produced unprompted offensive replies, such as calling the Holocaust 'made up' when asked; that Microsoft suspended the account within 16 hours, after more than 96,000 tweets; and that an accidental restart on 30 March 2016 left Tay stuck repeating 'you are too fast, please take a rest' into more than 200,000 followers' feeds before it was pulled a second time.
